$comment: TU Berlin building codes — SURVEYED, not invented, and unlike the OTH file not lifted from a website either. TU Berlin publishes its building codes (Raumfinder, campus plan) and OpenStreetMap has already recorded them on the outlines themselves, so the codes here are read straight off the same features the twin renders. That is a stronger link than OTH's: there the letters come from a PDF and have to be matched to an outline by name, here the code and the polygon are the same OSM object.
$provenance: Two OSM tags, and the difference is recorded rather than flattened. `ref` is the building code proper and is the preferred source. Where a building carries no `ref` but its `name` IS the code (TU Berlin labels many outlines simply 'MAR', 'TC', 'K'), the name is used. Anything that matches neither gets no entry here, and `generate_timetable.py` will give it a LOWER-CASE placeholder — which is what a lower-case code means anywhere in this dataset: ours, not the university's.
$osmNameToLetterNote: Keyed by the OSM `name`, because that is what `generate_timetable.py::building_rows` looks up. 'Hauptgebäude' -> 'H' is a name-to-ref mapping; 'MAR' -> 'MAR' is a code that is its own name.
